paper.abstract_en: This paper presents recent progress in the study of spin physics using BESIII data, focusing on two topics: hyperon physics and fragmentation functions.At BESIII, tens of millions of the spin-entangled hyperon-antihyperon pairs are produced in $J/\psi$ and $\psi(3686)$ decays. By analyzing these hyperon-antihyperon pairs, we observe transverse polarizations of $\Lambda$, $\Sigma^{+}$, $\Sigma^{0}$, and $\Xi^{0}$, $\Xi^{-}$,enabling precise tests of CP symmetry in hyperon decays.We report the measurements of normalized differential cross sections of inclusive $\pi^0$, $K^{0}_S$, $\pi^{\pm}$, $K^{\pm}$, and $\eta$ production as afunction of hadron momentum at different energy points. The results of $\pi^0$ and $K^{0}_S$ covering relative hadron energies from 0.1 to 0.9 significantly deviate from several theoretical calculations based on existing fragmentation functions.
